parts.title: Opinion Matching - Test 08
parts.instructions: Read the four texts. For each statement, choose the person (Person A, Person B, Person C, or Person D) who expresses that opinion.

people.name: Person A
people.biographyText: Four people respond to the request from the reporter asking about watching TV. Read their answers and answer the questions below.

people.name: Person B
people.biographyText: A In my house, the TV is always on, and I usually watch whatever is playing because it's my way of staying entertained. However, sometimes I come across a really interesting series, and I can’t stop following it. That’s how I entertain myself every day.

people.name: Person C
people.biographyText: B I was never good at school because my grades were always low. However, I can remember a lot of practical things from watching TV. For me, it’s a great way to expand my understanding of the world, and I believe it will be more useful when I graduate than the dry, theoretical knowledge we learn in school.

people.name: Person D
people.biographyText: C I don’t watch television much lately because I find most reality shows to be pretty stupid. I realized they’re all scripted, and the actors just follow a set plan. Once I learned that, I stopped watching those kinds of shows altogether. I switched to watching football instead, but my favorite team keeps losing, so I lost interest in that too.

parts.title: Matching Headings - Test 08
parts.instructions: Read the passage quickly. Choose a heading for each numbered paragraph (1-7) from the drop-down box.

paragraphs.text: Read the text. Match the headings to the paragraphs. There is one heading that you will not use.

1. There are several types of vegetarian diets. Some people avoid all animal products, like vegans, while others, like lacto-vegetarians, consume dairy products. There are also ovo-vegetarians, who include eggs in their diet. Many people follow a pescatarian diet, which includes fish but no other meat. Each of these diets offers a mwide variety of meals that are rich in fruits, vegetables, grains, and plant-based proteins.

2. The reasons behind dietary choices can be as diverse as the individuals themselves. Many people choose a vegetarian lifestyle for ethical reasons, environmental awareness, or health considerations. Others are influenced by cultural traditions or personal beliefs, while some are simply looking for new culinary experiences. Understanding these motivations can foster respectful discussions about food choices and promote a more inclusive dialogue around dietary preferences.

3. As the global population continues to grow, concerns about food security and sustainability are becoming more urgent. The increasing demand for resources places great pressure on agricultural systems, leading to potential shortages and higher food prices. Without significant changes in how we consume and produce food, we could soon face a serious crisis. This situation highlights the importance of more diverse dietary choices, including vegetarian diets, which can help ease the burden on global food systems.

4. The industrial approach to livestock production also raises important ethical and environmental concerns. Large-scale operations often prioritize efficiency over animal welfare, resulting in overcrowded conditions and the overuse of antibiotics. These practices not only affect the well-being of animals but also contribute to pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. As awareness of these issues increases, more people are advocating for humane and sustainable farming practices that align with the ethical values of plant-based diets.

5. In today’s interconnected world, our food choices have far-reaching consequences. Every individual's decisions can influence broader societal impacts, from environmental sustainability to animal welfare. Embracing a sense of stewardship encourages us to consider how our eating habits affect not only our health but also the health of the planet. By making conscious choices—such as incorporating more plant-based meals—we can work together toward a more equitable and sustainable future.

6. Opting for a diet rich in plant-based foods offers numerous advantages for overall well-being. Research suggests that consuming a variety of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and legumes can reduce the risk of chronic diseases such as heart disease and diabetes. These foods are typically high in essential nutrients and low in unhealthy fats. Embracing a more plant-centered way of eating supports personal health while also contributing to global sustainability efforts.
